newsitem.title: USA: Suspect in Florida heist still on loose.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Florida heist still on loose.

text.p: Police and federal agents were following tips from the public Saturday in a nationwide manhunt for the suspect in a heist and kidnapping at the security firm Loomis Fargo.

Media reports have put the haul at up to $20 million, which would make the theft one of the biggest in U.S. history. A reward of $500,000 was posted Friday for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the culprit.
Loomis armoured car driver Philip Noel Johnson, 37, was being sought on a state warrant for robbery and kidnapping and a federal warrant for unlawful flight, authorities said.
Johnson was charged with taking the money and kidnapping two co-workers at gunpoint in the March 29 heist at a Loomis office in Jacksonville.
He is considered "armed and dangerous" and was last seen driving a white van with Florida plates. The vehicle was recovered in Asheville, North Carolina, last Monday.
FBI special agent Bill Cheek said the reward had triggered a handful of tips from the public, but as of midday Saturday Johnson was still at large.
"We're getting phone calls and following them up," he said.

Police and FBI agents executed a search warrant at Johnson's abandoned Jacksonville home Thursday, seizing travel booklets, a bank bag, a handful of cash, an ammunition box and an ammunition clip commonly used for assault rifles, the Florida Times-Union newspaper reported.
One of the travel guides was titled "Dollarwise Brazil," the newspaper said.

The Times-Union said the robbery occurred between 6 p.m. and midnight March 29 as Johnson and fellow guards Dan Smith and James Brown were working. A co-worker told the newspaper that Smith and Brown had told him they were cleaning up the vault area when they were attacked at gunpoint.
"He used a gun to take the guns away from his fellow employees," Cheek confirmed Saturday.
Brown was taken to Johnson's home and handcuffed in a closet, and Smith, still wearing his uniform, was found wandering in the woods near Asheville, North Carolina, on Sunday, the newspaper said.
Loomis Fargo was formed in 1996 from the merger of armoured transport firms Loomis Armoured Inc and Wells Fargo Armoured Service.
